title: Ghost bytes in a zero-copy ring
subtitle: A pinned-memory ring deadlocked with the GPU idle and hundreds of thousands of items in flight, because wrap-around padding was never freed; and a GPU worker that registered twice was starved as dead

lede: Batches reach the GPU through a hot queue in pinned host memory: mapped, write-combined, pre-faulted pages holding a ring of batch descriptors, with a doorbell the producer rings to publish and the GPU waits on. No copies, no allocation after warm-up, and one accounting error that stopped two GPUs. When a batch does not fit before the end of the ring, the producer pads to the wrap point and writes the batch at the start. Every wrap left a few ghost bytes allocated and unreleasable, and over a long run they accumulated until the ring reported itself full with nothing in it, with a second consumer starving behind the first.
quote: Zero-copy and lock-free paths fail by accounting rather than by crashing, and the failures show up as a system that is quiet when it should be busy.
evidence: Lock-free and zero-copy data paths: a pinned-memory ring between CPU and GPU deadlocked by wrap-around padding never released, fixed by a padding field the acknowledgement returns.
Distributed systems debugging: a stall with 62,400 items dispatched and unresolved, 0 pending tokens and the GPU idle, traced to an accounting error rather than a crash.
Message broker and queue design: each GPU worker registered once on one socket split into read and write halves that fail together, so working GPUs stop being declared dead.
CUDA stream and event discipline: compute-stream synchronisation refused at run time and events drawn from a pool with generation counters and owner-thread checks, covered by 27 tests.
author: Corey James
